Adaptive line spacing from loaded bathymetry (wider lines in deeper water)

Adaptive mode needs depth data: global bathymetry (section {§gbath}) or your own XYZ soundings (section {§xyz}). Each line is placed as far from the previous one as the local depth allows while keeping the chosen overlap along its whole length. The swath is assumed to see flat seabed at the depth under the line, and the lines alternate direction (port/starboard angles swap).

The data are only as good as the source: GMRT and NCEI hold real multibeam surveys in places but are 100–450 m grids elsewhere, so use them for planning, not as a substitute for your own soundings. Land and drying cells are ignored. Vertical datum is roughly mean sea level, not chart datum: use the vertical offset in section {§xyz} or choose a conservative depth. If your browser blocks a service (offline or CORS), use the link shown to download the grid and load it here. Sources: GMRT (Lamont-Doherty), NOAA NCEI, EMODnet, GEBCO via Open Topo Data (1 request per second, 1000 per day).

A simplified a priori model after Hare (1995): range, angle (roll plus pointing), heave, water level, draft and sound speed for depth; positioning, heading, angle, pitch and sound speed for position. 95 % = 1.96σ vertical, 2.45σ horizontal. Check it against your own uncertainty model before you commit to a specification.
